segments.text: In the last week of October, the 27th to be precise, Sonia Gandhi said, there's bound to be some tamasha when the book comes out.
After all, others have spent decades telling my story.
Now it's my turn.
Well, on this account, she's spot on.
Of course, the jury is still out on the other accounts.
Congress party leaders call the book a love story, a story of resilience.
The BJP calls it whitewashing facts.
So is it an insider account or a carefully curated account for political gains?
Let's debate.
Joining me on India first is Dr. Shama Mohammed.
National spokesperson for the Congress Party.
Tuhin Sinha is national spokesperson for the Bharatiya Janata Party.
Professor Anand Ranganathan is author and consulting editor Swaraj Sanjay Jha.
Formerly with the Congress, he's met and interacted closely with Ten Janpa, joins us as an analyst.
Gentlemen and ladies, welcome.
Tuhin Sinha, Sonia Gandhi had a ringside view of political developments.
from the 1960s for over 60 years, be it wars, assassinations, including her mother-in-law and her husband, who feared he may be killed.
There was an apprehension.
Children may be kidnapped.
Rahul and Priyanka may be kidnapped.
That was the apprehension.
Why is her account being seen as whitewashing history, sir?
Well, good evening, Gaurav.
Good evening, everybody.
You know, first of all, let me extend my congratulations to Sonia Gandhiji on her autobiography or at least, you know, it's supposedly an autobiography.
But, you know, writing an autobiography requires a lot of moral courage and you should write it only when you are prepared to bear the truth.
completely.
Now there are several important aspects.
No doubt she has led a challenging life.
No doubt.
You know there have been humongous challenges along the way.
But I think you know the country also expects some very clear cut answers from her on contentious issues on mysterious issues.
And I think she should equally have addressed it.
For example, she came to India in 1968, but she acquired her citizenship formally in 1983.
But she is supposed to have voted in 1980.
There is a picture of hers casting her vote.
How did this happen?
Number two, you know, we are all interested in knowing what was the content of the secret MOU between Congress Party and CCP.
Number three, you know, Sonia Dandijee has been so upfront about, you know, shedding tears when Babri Masjid was demolished.
Salman Khurshid has gone a step forward and said, further and said, you know, she tried even when Patla House encounter took place.
The country also wants to know when all has she tried.
Has she tried when 26 11 happened or does she only cry when her port bank is in danger.
Has she tried when 74 CRPF Jawans were brutalized by by Naxals.
Or like I said she only gets worried when her port bank is in danger enough.
So you raise multiple points Dr. Shama Mohammed.

Her personal account may be very intense, yes, but her political commentary is being described as whitewashing the role of the Congress party, whether it's emergency or Punjab, Operation Blue Star, subsequent developments.
Is the congress party focusing on her personal life and does it face the risk of opening old wounds like Punjab being reignited?
Your take ma'am on what Tuhin Sinha said and my question ma'am.
So, Gaurav, this is a book, what is it called?
A Journey of Love, isn't it?

It's about a woman coming from somewhere else, from another country, coming to this country, accepting it, accepting the country, accepting the people, being with the people, married to the Nehru-Gandhi family,
did not want her husband to get into politics.
But even when he did, she stood by him.
She saw her mother-in-law assassinated in front of her eyes.
In fact, the bloody body of Indiraji was on her lap.
She took her to the hospital.
I mean, just try to think what all she's been through.
Then when her husband was assassinated, she's already gone through one, then she had her husband who was assassinated.
She was very close to, and the reason she is in this country of ours, she had to go through that.
And after that, she said, I am not going to be involved.
I'm going to stay away.
She was trying to get the Indira Gandhi's book on her and many other things she was doing.
But again, she was pressured to come.
as the president of the Communist Party.
And must say, when she came in, she could lead.
She learned the language.
And she was leading the country.
And we won in 2004.
There were people who left the party at that point.
Certain leaders were upset and called her names.
But they've all come back.
They were with us in the UPA, one, as well as two.
So what we understand is she's a person

who believes India first, Indian people, all of India, whether they are Sikhs, whether they're Hindus, Muslims, Christians, you know, she's not a divisive person, as you know, when she was there, she's a consensus, a politician, a leader, where consensus comes first, and a lot of love, because I have known her, and when I have met her also,
She listens to you.
She is somebody, as a politician, you speak more and she listens.
She's very empathetic.
She's very concerned about you.

And how can, you know, how is a woman, especially when it comes to women, as a woman, I can stand by because the ones who got the women's reservation bill in 2008, we could pass it in the Rajya Sabha, not in the Lok Sabha.
So there were issues because of that.
Otherwise we would have done it long time back and we didn't have a caveat.
Let's understand.
We didn't say that.
Let me bring in Anand Ranganathan, because for the moment, we're staying with the book and commentary around it.
Anand Ranganathan, Sonia Gandhi had a ringside view of developments in the prime minister's residence.
She's recounting what she saw.
Is this allegation or this complaint that she's whitewashing events, is that an unfair criticism of Amma Maharsha?
Good evening Gaurav and good evening to my fellow panelists.
Well, you know, as they say, you either see what you believe or you believe what you see.
And in Mrs. Gandhi's case, Sonia Gandhi's case, I'm afraid the pen with which she has written her memoirs is dipped not in ink, but in Harpic.
She has ruthlessly tried to vishvash and scrub, not just whitewash.
the history right before our very eyes.
Each and every instance that you describe, that is in her fictionalized book, is a complete negation of history.
She is trying to whitewash the crimes and misdemeanors of her close associates.
For example, shamelessly apportioning blame of the emergency
from Indira Gandhi to Sanjay Gandhi.
And I am surprised that Menaka Gandhi has not yet spoken out.
This is an absolute crime when she says that emergency was thrust principally by on the behalf of Sanjay Gandhi.
It is a calamity.
Hundreds and thousands were interned, millions were sterilized, thousands were killed.
all this happened right under the command and directions of Indira Gandhi.
For somebody to say that Sanjay Gandhi is responsible for this, it is in front of our eyes, brushing the history in front of us.
Secondly, does this memoir mention about what Rajiv Gandhi said about the Sikhs?
the genocide of the Sikhs in 1984 in the wake of the assassination is right on the shoulders of Rajiv Gandhi.
Has that been mentioned by Sonia Gandhi?
Have both of them ever apologized for what happened for the emergency and for the 1984 Sikh genocide?
So, you know, yes, she is within her right to write whatever she wants to, but this is a deeply sanitized, scrubbed-out version of history before us, Gaurav.
Let's be honest about it.
Let me get Sanjay Jha to respond.
Sanjay Jha, this is not history that's written with pen and ink.
It's actually scrubbed with pen and Harpick, says Professor Ranganathan, or what's to that effect?
Let's take this one by one.
Emergency, for example, that's described as the darkest chapter in post-independence India.
BJP says Sonia Gandhi is whitewashing Indira Gandhi's role and blaming Sanjay Gandhi for emergency, or what's to that effect?
How fair is that criticism, sir?
I got a good evening to you now.
First and foremost, this is a memoir.

of a person who was dead and saw it from her perspective to her experience of seeing what was going on at the highest level of political decision making for Anand Ranganathan of the BGP to challenge that is rather ridiculous.
It's like me saying that right now I'm sitting here in Pune and I can see a lizard on the wall and Anand Ranganathan said that's not a lizard that's a dinosaur.
It's a ridiculous argument.
Let's not go down that road.
This is an individual's personal memoir.
Now you can challenge it by another memoir and you can come up with a fact.
But these rhetoric and these you know cheap gibberish comments have no meaning.
I'm going to bite the bullet on your program.
I have my friend Shama here who's who's anyway doing some brilliant heavy lifting already.
But let me just come to the point ASAP.
OK.
And I'm going to bite the bullet.
God of how you started the Babri must demolition because I have been part of several debates when I have been officially part of the Congress as a spokesperson.
Let me remind you who's whitewashing.
Let me tell you nothing.
And I'm not going to quote a politician.
I'm going to quote
an esteemed Supreme Court lawyer, Manmohan Singh Lagerhand Commission's report.
No whitewashing.
And this is a fact that the viewer should know.
You know, the Commission concluded that the Babri-Masjid demolition was not a spontaneous mob violence as the BJP would like India to believe, but it was a methodical and meticulously planned
civil conspiracy to bring down the entire mosque.
Now more important more important the Library Commission indicted the Sankt Paribas VHP artists BJP Bajrang Dal everybody for taking part in the entire methodical demolition.
Most importantly it actually held leaders of the BJP.
Mr. L.K.
Adwani with due respects to his age.
Murali Manohar Joshi due respects to his age.
Uma Bharti in fact accepted her responsibility as people responsible for what really went on.
And guess what it called the BJP and the Sangh Parivar pseudo moderates
who carried intellectual responsibility for the event.
Where will Anand and Tuhin Sinha go into hiding now?
I'll get both of them to respond, but since you specifically mentioned Anand Ranganathan's name, I'm getting Anand Ranganathan to respond to you, and then Tuhin Sinha on the political point of L.K.
Advani and others.
Before I bring in Shambha Muhammad, go ahead, Professor Ranganathan.
First of all, with due respect to my good friend Sanjay, it's a specious argument.
Of course, I myself said it.
It's a memoir.
It's her point of view, and it's a deeply sanitized point of view.
But I have seen and read history of that time.
The fact of the matter is, as I said, she's open to interpret or say what happened right before us.
Of course she is.
But I'm disputing the facts.
that she is putting out, that Indira Gandhi was responsible for the emergency, not Sanjay Gandhi.
Sanjay Gandhi took part in the atrocities that followed the declaration of emergency, but the proclamation of it, because I've written on it, and I've read books on it.
The fact of the matter is, Indira Gandhi is to be blamed for emergency, let's not take away that blame from it.
As far as the Babri Masjid demolition is concerned, for her to, you know, whatever she says, she's free to her opinion.
I can't dispute that, obviously.
No, if she cried on that, if she cried on Batra encounter where a terrorist was killed, that's her opinion.
I'm not disputing that.
But I myself have condemned the demolition of Babri Masjid, and I'll say this.
for 15 of the 30-35 years that have gone past the demolition, Congress was in power, CBI was controlled by them.
Why was Adwani not put under arrest?
Why was Murali Manohar Jaspur under arrest?
Why did Mulayam Singh say there was no evidence against Adwani?
So let's not... What do they say?
Run with the hair and hunt with the hounds.

You did, for obvious reasons.
Fair enough.
And I will get Dr. Shama Mohammed also to respond to this aspect.

But, Tuhin Sinha, respond.

thought of or tried to build, blame is on BJP RSS.
No, no, I understand.
Sonia Gandhi is a very emotional person.
You know, so she keeps, she gets to, she tries often.
But my point is only, you know, she never mentions about trying at the, when, when, you know, 74 of her CRP of Jawans get killed or when 26-11 happens.

Now I would have at least expected the two Congress representatives to be given the book one week or 10 days before so that they don't come up with these cliched arguments and, you know, BJP bashing, which they are very good at.
But my point is very simple.
Does the country not have the right to know why it took Sonia Gandhiji 10 days after the nuclear test in May 1998 to come up with the first reaction?
And even that first reaction was a cavalier.
India's strength lies in restraint.
without understanding the situation.
Does India not have the right to know from Sonia Gandhi why India did not go after Pakistan despite a string of bomb blasts, series of bomb blasts right between 2004 and 2009 every 40 days?
I'm expecting answers to these serious questions.
Fair enough.

Sonia Gandhi writes about being in tears when Babri Masjid and what the BJP describes as their disputed structure was demolished.

How would you respond to this criticism?
I think you'll have to unmute yourself, ma'am.

Mrs. Gandhi has had tears in her eyes many times.
She has tears.

How did we not go against Pakistan when Patankot happened?

We never did something as stupid as that.
So let's understand.
Manmohan Singh, for 10 years, Soniaji, none of them visited Pakistan.

All right.
